text: Charles Allen Parker Bartlett was an American politician from Pennsylvania who served in the Pennsylvania State Senate, representing the 18th district from 1939 to 1942. The 18th district covered Northampton County, Pennsylvania. Born in Concord, Massachusetts, on November 17, 1880, to Charles H. Bartlett and Mary A. Née Hobson, Bartlett moved to Easton, Pennsylvania, where he completed a public high school education and did not attend college. From 1904 to 1933, he worked as a secretary, treasurer, and sales agent for local manufacturing firms. He joined the Pennsylvania National Guard in 1904 and during World War I, served as a Captain commanding Company A of the Rainbow Division's 149th Machine Gun Battalion within the American Expeditionary Forces from 1917 to 1919. After the war, he served as a Major in the Pennsylvania National Guard's coastal artillery until 1923. Following his military service, Bartlett was elected president of Wilson, Pennsylvania, for four years and served as the borough's Treasurer for nine years before being elected to the Pennsylvania State Senate from 1939 to 1942, during which he chaired the welfare committee. He then served as the Pennsylvania Senate Librarian from 1943 to 1948. Bartlett married Mildred E. Née Richards. He died on March 18, 1948, in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, at the age of 67, and is buried in Sleepy Hollow Cemetery in his native Concord.
